version.changelog: Payer accepts the documented x402 v1 network shorthand ("base") as an alias for eip155:8453, which is what most v1 sellers advertise - buyers no longer need to normalise it by hand. Authorization is still built for eip155:8453 only; unknown shorthands are still refused. Also: package carries no build artefacts.

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed pay-per-call client that can spend USDC only when the user provides a payer key and explicitly runs the pay command.

dimensions.detail: Network access, route bodies, wallet address lookups, and payment signatures are proportionate to buying x402 data, but users should treat submitted documents, URLs, wallet addresses, and prompts as data sent to external services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation requires Python packages x402 and eth_account, but there are no install scripts, persistence hooks, shell wrappers, or automatic setup actions in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are user-directed CLI workflows for catalogue, quote, whoami, and pay; I found no session hijacking, hidden role changes, automatic execution, or prompt-injection behavior in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script reads only XH_PAYER_KEY or the file named by XH_PAYER_KEY_FILE for paid modes, performs no filesystem writes, does not mutate the environment, and does not install services or long-running workers.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capability is high impact because it reads a wallet private key and can move USDC, but that is the stated purpose and is prominently disclosed with price, asset, network, and payTo guardrails.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in an environment where a dedicated, low-balance Base wallet key may be read by the process and used to spend USDC. Quote before paying, keep the default or lower --max ceiling, use --pay-to when possible, and do not send private documents, internal URLs, credentials, or sensitive prompts to the paid routes unless you accept the external service handling that data.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The Google Drive and YouTube automation entries are catalogue descriptions for paid routes; they may involve sensitive account-linked workflows, but the artifact does not hide that they are external paid calls. This is a privacy guidance issue rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The web-search route explicitly describes web search and page retrieval, so outbound retrieval is expected. Users should still avoid submitting private URLs, tokens, or sensitive content because the catalogue does not provide detailed retention or logging terms.
[AST7] expected: The getattr use is limited to a fixed allowlist of model serialization method names, model_dump and dict, for normalizing SDK objects; it is not used to execute arbitrary code or access user-selected attributes.
